01.actor: Rav Avya and his wife, the sister of Rami bar Hama
01.event: Her marriage contract was lost and the couple came before Rav Yosef to ask what to do.
01.turn: Rav Yosef first said the Rabbis allow a man to live with his wife for years without a contract, but Abaye objected that the halakha follows Rabbi Meir's decrees.
01.outcome: Rav Yosef told them to go and write her a new marriage contract.
01.summary: Rav Avya was married to the sister of Rami bar Hama, and her marriage contract was lost. They asked Rav Yosef, who cited the view that a man may go two or three years without one. Abaye objected that the law follows Rabbi Meir, who is strict about this. Rav Yosef then told them to go and write her a new contract.

02.actor: Rabbi Yohanan and Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat
02.event: Rabbi Elazar silenced Rabbi Yohanan with an objection to his teaching about burning leftover sacrificial meat.
02.turn: Rabbi Yohanan praised the exposition as if from Moses, but Reish Lakish revealed it was really a baraita from Torat Kohanim.
02.outcome: Rabbi Yohanan went and learned Torat Kohanim in three days and mastered it in three months.
02.summary: Rabbi Yohanan was teaching when Rabbi Elazar raised an objection from a baraita, and Rabbi Yohanan had no answer. Afterwards he told Reish Lakish that Ben Pedat expounded like Moses receiving the Torah from God. Reish Lakish said it was not his own idea but a baraita in Torat Kohanim. Rabbi Yohanan then learned that whole work in three days and understood it in three months.

03.actor: a tumtum (person of indeterminate sex) in the town of Biri
03.event: He was operated on so that his genitals were opened, and he later fathered seven children.
03.turn: The case is cited against Rabbi Yehuda, who would reply that the children's paternity is doubtful.
03.summary: A person of indeterminate sex living in Biri was seated for an operation and had his genitals opened, and he later had seven children. Rabbi Ami cites the case to challenge Rabbi Yehuda's view that such a person is impotent; Rabbi Yehuda's answer would be to question where the children came from.
03.missing: The case is only cited as an argument; nothing further happens to the man in the text.

04.actor: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin (or Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Zevida), and Ameimar
04.event: A visiting sage ruled on the status of children born to women who had relations with a slave.
04.turn: The reports disagree on who the sage was and whether he declared the married woman's child unfit.
04.outcome: Ameimar, on a visit, declared such children fit in both cases.
04.summary: Rav Gazza reported that a visiting sage once ruled the child of an unmarried woman and a slave fit to marry, but the child of a married woman unfit. Another version says the visitor was a different sage who ruled both children fit. Ameimar, visiting another town, also ruled both fit.
04.missing: The incidents are reported only as rulings; no details of the people involved.

05.actor: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda, Marei bar Mar, Rav Huna and his son Rabba
05.event: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda sent Marei bar Mar to ask Rav Huna whether the halakha follows Rabbi Elazar on bills of divorce.
05.turn: Before the question arrived, Rav Huna died.
05.outcome: Rav Huna's son Rabba answered in his father's name that the halakha follows Rabbi Elazar.
05.summary: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda sent a request to Marei bar Mar to ask Rav Huna a legal question about bills of divorce. In the meantime Rav Huna died. His son Rabba answered instead, reporting that his father, and other learned teachers in Rav's name, held that the halakha follows Rabbi Elazar.

06.actor: a man who left a dowry to his daughter, and his heirs
06.event: A man's will instructed his heirs to give his daughter a dowry, and dowry prices then fell.
06.turn: The question arose who gets the difference between the intended and the actual cost.
06.outcome: Rav Idi bar Avin ruled the saving goes to the male orphans.
06.summary: A man instructed his heirs to give his daughter a dowry, but before it was given the cost of dowries dropped. Rav Idi bar Avin ruled that the money saved belongs to the sons, not the daughter.
06.missing: Only the legal facts and ruling are given; no further development.

07.actor: a woman holding a bag of documents
07.event: Heirs demanded a bag of documents deposited with her, and she claimed she had seized it from the deceased while he was alive.
07.turn: Rav Nahman asked for witnesses that the deceased had demanded it in his lifetime and she refused, and she had none.
07.outcome: He ruled her seizure was after death and therefore worthless.
07.summary: A woman had a bag of documents deposited with her, and after the owner died his heirs claimed it. She said she had seized it during his lifetime to cover a debt. Rav Nahman asked if she had witnesses that the owner had demanded it while alive and she refused; she had none, so he ruled it counted as seizure after death, which is invalid.

08.actor: a man in love with a woman (reported in a letter from Rabba's brothers)
08.event: A man suffering from love for a woman wanted to leave the Land of Israel to be with her.
08.turn: He heard the teaching about the importance of living in the Land of Israel.
08.outcome: He stayed and suffered until the day he died.
08.summary: Rabba's brothers wrote to him from the Land of Israel, quoting Ilfa's story of a man who was suffering for love of a woman and wished to leave the land. When he heard how important it is to stay in the Land of Israel, he stayed and endured his suffering until he died. The rest of the letter urges Rabba to come and gives health advice.
08.missing: The anecdote is told in a few words; the rest of the passage is advice, not narrative.

09.actor: an unmarried man who came before Rav Nahman
09.event: A man claimed before Rav Nahman that he found his bride's virginity absent.
09.turn: Rav Nahman realized that an inexperienced bachelor could only know this from consorting with prostitutes.
09.outcome: He ordered the man flogged with palm branches.
09.summary: A man who had never been married came to Rav Nahman and claimed that his new wife was not a virgin. Rav Nahman reasoned that he could only know this if he had been with prostitutes. He ordered that the man be flogged with palm branches.

10.event: Rabbi Tavla visited Mehoza and saw a door bolt hanging beside the door, not tied to it.
10.summary: Rabbi Tavla came to Mehoza and saw a door bolt hanging from the side of a door. He made no objection to the people there. The Gemara explains that this bolt could be lifted by its rope.
10.missing: The incident is cited only as a legal precedent; there is no development or ending.

11.actor: a woman selling belts and a man who snatched one
11.event: A man grabbed a belt from a woman selling them and asked if she would be betrothed to him if he gave it back.
11.turn: She took the belt and said nothing.
11.outcome: Rav Nahman ruled she was not betrothed, since she could say she was only taking back her own property.
11.summary: A woman was selling belts when a man snatched one from her. When she demanded it back, he asked whether she would be betrothed to him if he returned it. She took it in silence. Rav Nahman ruled that her silence meant nothing, because she was simply taking back what was hers.

12.actor: the wife (widow) of Rav Yosef son of Rava
12.event: She came before Rav Nehemya asking him to set her allowance for food and then for wine.
12.turn: He granted wine, explaining that the people of Mehoza drink wine.
12.outcome: She received both sustenance and wine.
12.summary: The wife of Rav Yosef son of Rava came before Rav Nehemya and asked him to fix her food allowance, which he did. She then asked for wine as well. He granted it, saying he knew the people of Mehoza drink wine.

16.event: Rabbi Hiyya and Bar Kappara each jumped up and swore by the Temple service that they had heard opposite rulings from Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.
16.turn: Unable to settle it by tradition, each began to argue it by reasoning, and the same clash repeated over three cases.
16.summary: Rabbi Hiyya and Bar Kappara disagreed about how many counts a person is liable for in several Temple cases. Each leapt up and swore by the Temple service that he had heard his version from Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi. Each then argued his view from reasoning, and the scene repeated for three different cases. The rest is the Gemara's legal analysis of their dispute.
16.missing: The confrontation has no resolution; the text moves into legal analysis.

17.actor: the Israelites after the war with Midian
17.event: To tell which captive girls were of age, they passed them before the High Priest's frontplate.
17.turn: The faces of those who were of age miraculously turned pale.
17.summary: The Gemara asks how the Israelites knew which Midianite girls were of age. Rabbi Shimon Hasida explains that they were passed before the High Priest's frontplate, and those whose faces turned pale were known to be of age.
17.missing: This is an explanatory gloss on a biblical episode; the episode itself is not told.

19.event: Nehemya was so absorbed in his learning that he walked beyond the Shabbat boundary.
19.turn: Rav Hisda told Rav Nahman his student was stuck and in distress.
19.outcome: Rav Nahman said to form a partition of people so he could walk back in.
19.summary: Nehemya, son of Rav Hanilai, was so engrossed in his studies on Shabbat that he wandered past the boundary he was allowed to walk. Rav Hisda told Rav Nahman that his student was stuck outside. Rav Nahman told him to line people up to form a human wall so Nehemya could walk back inside it.
